steps.body: Fill a frame from a teen-sized pile and some dots will not fit. Those LEFTOVERS are exactly the ones digit, sorted out for you.
steps.narration: Fill a frame from a teen-sized pile and some dots will not fit. Those LEFTOVERS are exactly the ones digit, sorted out for you.

widget.prompt: A full group of 10 is already shown. Add the extra dots needed to make 17.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 7 dots still missing — the ten alone only makes 10, not 17.
6 leaves 1 dot still missing; ten and 6 is 16, one short of 17.
8 adds 1 too many; ten and 8 is 18, one past 17.

widget.missFeedback: The ten is done; count on from 10 while adding dots, and stop when you reach 17.
widget.successFeedback: 17 built — one complete ten and 7 more, exactly what the teen numeral says.

predict.prompt: 17 dots meet a ten-frame. How many stay outside?
predict.reveal: The frame holds exactly ten; the ones digit counts everything past that.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb leftover ones.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb leftover ones rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: 19 dots fill one ten-frame with some left outside. How many are left over?

options.label: 9 — the ten is inside, the rest ride outside
options.feedback: Correct — 19 is one full ten and 9 ones, so exactly 9 dots cannot fit in the frame.

options.label: 19 — all of them are left over
options.feedback: Ten of the nineteen sit INSIDE the frame; only the ones beyond the ten remain out.

options.label: 10 — the frame's worth
options.feedback: The frame's ten is the part that fits; the leftovers are what exceeds it.

options.label: 1 — just one dot
options.feedback: One would make eleven in all; nineteen carries nine past the completed ten.

commonCounts.feedback: That shows one too few loose ones. The target needs 8.

widget.missFeedback: Keep the full ten fixed and build exactly 8 loose ones.

widget.prompt: A group shows 13 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: That numeral names one more dot than the group shows.
Correct — a full ten and 3 more is what the numeral 13 says: 1 ten, 3 ones.
That numeral stops one dot short; the ten plus the extras reaches 13.
3 counts only the extras and forgets the whole completed ten underneath.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 8. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 17 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 18.
19 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 8 hops from 10 to land on 18.

widget.missFeedback: Count 8 on from 10: you land on 18.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 8 more is 18 — the teen numeral written as a walk: ten first, then the ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 8 counts past ten are needed to reach 18.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 8 numbers, on 18.

widget.prompt: A frame shows a full ten and 7 outside. Which teen is it?

options.label: 17 — ten and seven
options.feedback: Correct — one complete ten and 7 ones is exactly what the numeral 17 records.

options.label: 7 — just the outsiders
options.feedback: Counting only the extras drops the completed ten; the whole group is ten and seven.

options.label: 70 — seven and a zero
options.feedback: 70 means seven TENS; here there is one ten and seven ones, which is 17.

options.label: 10 — the frame alone
options.feedback: The frame's ten is only part of the group; the 7 outside push the total to 17.
